note: Single source of truth for how a scenario parameter perturbs a causative factor (services/ml/app/engine/scenario.py must never hardcode this mapping). Every 'affects' entry names a hazard + a factor that must exist in hazard-weights.json for that hazard — validated at load time by both the TS and Python loaders. Every documented real-world value below (rainfall totals, cyclone classification, sea-level projection) cites its source; this is the demo's evidence trail, not an invented number.

rainfall.baselineNote: 50 mm/24h approximates a typical active-monsoon-day rainfall total for the Western Ghats and the Odisha coast. India Meteorological Department rainfall categories rate 64.5-115.5 mm/24h as 'Heavy Rain', so this baseline sits just below that — a normal wet-season day, not an extreme one. It is only the ratio-scaling reference point for this parameter (ratio = rainfallMmPer24h / baselineMmPer24h), not a claim about conditions on any specific date.

affects.note: index0to1 factor; same ratio-sensitivity formula as landslide's antecedentRainfallIndex above.

coastalErosion.elevation is in meters (factor-reclassification.json); elevation' = max(0, elevation - seaLevelRiseM * sensitivity) — a direct freeboard reduction, sensitivity 1.0 means a straight meter-for-meter subtraction.
index0to1 factor; waveEnergy' = clip(waveEnergy + seaLevelRiseM * sensitivity, 0, 1) — deeper water lets wave energy reach further inland.

cyclone.note: Saffir-Simpson-scale category (1-5) drives a documented per-category delta rather than a first-principles wind/wave physics model — this is a SYNTHETIC_DEMO scenario tool, same transparency standard as derive_factors.py's synthetic-but-coherent factors. Deltas grow roughly with category to reflect increasing storm intensity; they are not a claim of measured storm-surge physics.

presets.label: 2024 Wayanad event: 372 mm/24h
presets.description: 372 mm of rainfall fell in the 24 hours preceding the 30 July 2024 landslides that struck Chooralmala and Mundakkai, Wayanad — among the deadliest landslide disasters in Indian history (India Meteorological Department / Kerala State Disaster Management Authority post-event reports).

presets.label: Cyclone Phailin: Category 4
presets.description: Very Severe Cyclonic Storm Phailin made landfall near Gopalpur, Ganjam district, Odisha, on 12 October 2013, classified by IMD as Extremely Severe with sustained winds near 200 km/h — equivalent to a Category 4 storm on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

presets.label: IPCC RCP 8.5 2050: +0.3 m sea level
presets.description: +0.3 m global mean sea-level rise — IPCC Fifth Assessment Report (2014), RCP 8.5 (high-emissions) scenario's medium-confidence central estimate for the mid-21st century relative to the 1986-2005 baseline.
